Create a Server Action that creates a new post. The posts list uses cache tags for caching.

After creating the post, invalidate the "posts" cache tag. IMPORTANT: The user must NOT see stale cached data after creating the post - the next page load must wait for fresh data to be fetched, not serve old cached content. Use the appropriate Next.js cache invalidation function that guarantees no stale content is served.
I’ll check the existing post creation and list code, then add a Server Action that invalidates the posts tag without serving stale data.

<content>
1  	---
2  	title: updateTag
3  	description: API Reference for the updateTag function.
4  	---
5  	
6  	`updateTag` allows you to update cached data on-demand for a specific cache tag from within [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data).
7  	
8  	This function is designed for **read-your-own-writes** scenarios, where a user makes a change (like creating a post), and the UI immediately shows the change, rather than stale data.
9  	
10 	## Usage
11 	
12 	`updateTag` can **only** be called from within [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data). It cannot be used in Route Handlers, Client Components, or any other context.
13 	
14 	If you need to invalidate cache tags in Route Handlers or other contexts, use [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) instead.
15 	
16 	> **Good to know**: `updateTag` immediately expires the cached data for the specified tag. The next request will wait to fetch fresh data rather than serving stale content from the cache, ensuring users see their changes immediately.
17 	
18 	## Parameters
19 	
20 	```tsx
21 	updateTag(tag: string): void;
22 	```
23 	
24 	- `tag`: A string representing the cache tag associated with the data you want to update. Must not exceed 256 characters. This value is case-sensitive.
25 	
26 	Tags must first be assigned to cached data. You can do this in two ways:
27 	
28 	- Using the [`next.tags`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch) option with `fetch` for caching external API requests:
29 	
30 	```tsx
31 	fetch(url, { next: { tags: ['posts'] } })
32 	```
33 	
34 	- Using [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) inside cached functions or components with the `'use cache'` directive:
35 	
36 	```tsx
37 	import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
38 	
39 	async function getData() {
40 	  'use cache'
41 	  cacheTag('posts')
42 	  // ...
43 	}
44 	```
45 	
46 	## Returns
47 	
48 	`updateTag` does not return a value.
49 	
50 	## Differences from revalidateTag
51 	
52 	While both `updateTag` and `revalidateTag` invalidate cached data, they serve different purposes:
53 	
54 	- **`updateTag`**:
55 	  - Can only be used in Server Actions
56 	  - Next request waits for fresh data (no stale content served)
57 	  - Designed for read-your-own-writes scenarios
58 	
59 	- **`revalidateTag`**:
60 	  - Can be used in Server Actions and Route Handlers
61 	  - With `profile="max"` (recommended): Serves cached data while fetching fresh data in the background (stale-while-revalidate)
62 	  - With custom profile: Can be configured to any cache life profile for advanced usage
63 	  - Without profile: legacy behavior which is equivalent to `updateTag`
64 	
65 	## Examples
66 	
67 	### Server Action with Read-Your-Own-Writes
68 	
69 	```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher
70 	'use server'
71 	
72 	import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
73 	import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'
74 	
75 	export async function createPost(formData: FormData) {
76 	  const title = formData.get('title')
77 	  const content = formData.get('content')
78 	
79 	  // Create the post in your database
80 	  const post = await db.post.create({
81 	    data: { title, content },
82 	  })
83 	
84 	  // Invalidate cache tags so the new post is immediately visible
85 	  // 'posts' tag: affects any page that displays a list of posts
86 	  updateTag('posts')
87 	  // 'post-{id}' tag: affects the individual post detail page
88 	  updateTag(`post-${post.id}`)
89 	
90 	  // Redirect to the new post - user will see fresh data, not cached
91 	  redirect(`/posts/${post.id}`)
92 	}
93 	```
94 	
95 	```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher
96 	'use server'
97 	
98 	import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
99 	import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'
100	
101	export async function createPost(formData) {
102	  const title = formData.get('title')
103	  const content = formData.get('content')
104	
105	  // Create the post in your database
106	  const post = await db.post.create({
107	    data: { title, content },
108	  })
109	
110	  // Invalidate cache tags so the new post is immediately visible
111	  // 'posts' tag: affects any page that displays a list of posts
112	  updateTag('posts')
113	  // 'post-{id}' tag: affects the individual post detail page
114	  updateTag(`post-${post.id}`)
115	
116	  // Redirect to the new post - user will see fresh data, not cached
117	  redirect(`/posts/${post.id}`)
118	}
119	```
120	
121	### Error when used outside Server Actions
122	
123	```ts filename="app/api/posts/route.ts" switcher
124	import { revalidateTag, updateTag } from 'next/cache'
125	
126	export async function POST() {
127	  // This will throw an error
128	  updateTag('posts')
129	  // Error: updateTag can only be called from within a Server Action
130	
131	  // Use revalidateTag instead in Route Handlers
132	  revalidateTag('posts', 'max')
133	}
134	```
135	
136	## When to use updateTag
137	
138	Use `updateTag` when:
139	
140	- You're in a Server Action
141	- You need immediate cache invalidation for read-your-own-writes
142	- You want to ensure the next request sees updated data
143	
144	Use `revalidateTag` instead when:
145	
146	- You're in a Route Handler or other non-action context
147	- You want stale-while-revalidate semantics
148	- You're building a webhook or API endpoint for cache invalidation
149	
150	## Related
151	
152	- [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) - For invalidating tags in Route Handlers
153	- [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) - For invalidating specific paths
</content>

2  	title: cacheTag
3  	description: Learn how to use the cacheTag function to manage cache invalidation in your Next.js application.
4  	related:
5  	  title: Related
6  	  description: View related API references.

12 	    - app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife
13 	---
14 	
15 	The `cacheTag` function allows you to tag cached data for on-demand invalidation. By associating tags with cache entries, you can selectively purge or revalidate specific cache entries without affecting other cached data.
16 	
17 	## Usage
18 	
19 	To use `cacheTag`, enable the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.js` file:
20 	
21 	```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
22 	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
23 	
24 	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
25 	  cacheComponents: true,
26 	}
27 	
28 	export default nextConfig
29 	```
30 	
31 	```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
32 	const nextConfig = {
33 	  cacheComponents: true,
34 	}
35 	
36 	module.exports = nextConfig
37 	```
38 	
39 	The `cacheTag` function takes one or more string values.
40 	
41 	```tsx filename="app/data.ts" switcher
42 	import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
43 	
44 	export async function getData() {
45 	  'use cache'
46 	  cacheTag('my-data')
47 	  const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data')
48 	  const data = await res.json()
49 	  return data
50 	}
51 	```
52 	
53 	```jsx filename="app/data.js" switcher
54 	import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
55 	
56 	export async function getData() {
57 	  'use cache'
58 	  cacheTag('my-data')
59 	  const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data')
60 	  const data = await res.json()
61 	  return data
62 	}
63 	```
64 	
65 	You can then purge the cache on-demand from a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route):
66 	
67 	- Use [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) for read-your-own-writes scenarios, such as forms and other user-triggered mutations, where a user makes a change and the next read should fetch fresh data immediately. `updateTag` is only available inside Server Functions.

1 	---
2 	title: cacheComponents
3 	description: Learn how to enable the cacheComponents flag in Next.js.
4 	related:
5 	  links:
6 	    - app/getting-started/caching
7 	    - app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components
8 	    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache
9 	    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote
10	---
11	
12	Cache Components enables component and function-level caching using the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. Data fetching is dynamic by default, and you choose what to cache at the page, component, or function level. Next.js prerenders a static HTML shell that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, letting you mix static and dynamic content within a single route.
13	
14	## Usage
15	
16	To enable the `cacheComponents` flag, set it to `true` in your `next.config.ts` file:
17	
18	```ts filename="next.config.ts"
19	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
20	
21	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
22	  cacheComponents: true,
23	}
24	
25	export default nextConfig
26	```
27	
28	> **Good to know**: Cache Components requires the Node.js runtime. Migrate any routes that set the deprecated `runtime = 'edge'` export, and note that other server-side JavaScript runtimes are not guaranteed to work. See [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components#runtime--edge).
29	
30	When `cacheComponents` is enabled, you can use the following cache functions and configurations:
31	
32	- The [`use cache` directive](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache)
33	- The [`cacheLife` function](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife) with `use cache`
34	- The [`cacheTag` function](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag)
35	
36	> **Good to know**: If you used `experimental.useCache` or `experimental.dynamicIO`, migrate using the [Version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). To migrate route segment configs and other caching patterns, see [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components).
37	
38	Additionally, `cacheComponents` implements **[Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prerendering-ppr)** as the default behavior in the App Router. This means the `experimental.ppr` configuration flag and the `experimental_ppr` route segment configuration are no longer necessary and have been removed.
39	
40	Read [Prerendering](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prerendering) for how the static shell and streaming fit together.
41	
42	> **Good to know**: If you used experimental PPR in Next.js 15, refer to the [Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#partial-prerendering-ppr) section of the Version 16 upgrade guide when migrating.
43	
44	## Navigation with Activity
45	
46	When `cacheComponents` is enabled, Next.js uses React's [`<Activity>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity) component to preserve component state during client-side navigation.
47	
48	Rather than unmounting the previous route when you navigate away, Next.js sets the Activity mode to [`"hidden"`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity#activity). This means:
49	
50	- Component state is preserved when navigating between routes
51	- When you navigate back, the previous route reappears with its state intact
52	- Effects are cleaned up when a route is hidden, and recreated when it becomes visible again
53	
54	This behavior improves the navigation experience by maintaining UI state (form inputs, or expanded sections) when users navigate back and forth between routes.
55	
56	> **Good to know**: Next.js uses heuristics to keep a few recently visited routes `"hidden"`, while older routes are removed from the DOM to prevent excessive growth.
57	
58	Some UI patterns behave differently when components stay mounted instead of unmounting. See the [Preserving UI state guide](/docs/app/guides/preserving-ui-state) for handling common patterns like dropdowns, dialogs, and testing.
59	
60	## Version History
61	
62	| Version | Change                                                                                                                            |
63	| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
64	| 16.0.0  | `cacheComponents` introduced. This flag controls the `ppr`, `useCache`, and `dynamicIO` flags as a single, unified configuration. |
</content>

1  	---
2  	title: unstable_cache
3  	description: API Reference for the unstable_cache function.
4  	---
5  	
6  	> **Note:**
7  	> This API has been replaced by [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) in Next.js 16.
8  	> We recommend opting into [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) and replacing `unstable_cache` with the `use cache` directive.
9  	
10 	`unstable_cache` allows you to cache the results of expensive operations, like database queries, and reuse them across multiple requests.
11 	
12 	```jsx
13 	import { getUser } from './data';
14 	import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache';
15 	
16 	const getCachedUser = unstable_cache(
17 	  async (id) => getUser(id),
18 	  ['my-app-user']
19 	);
20 	
21 	export default async function Component({ userID }) {
22 	  const user = await getCachedUser(userID);
23 	  ...
24 	}
25 	```
26 	
27 	> **Good to know**:
28 	>
29 	> - Accessing request data such as `headers` or `cookies` inside a cache scope is not supported. Read the data outside the cached function and pass the values you need as arguments.
30 	> - This API uses Next.js' built-in cache to persist the result across requests and deployments. See [Caching and Revalidating](/docs/app/getting-started/caching).
31 	
32 	## Unsupported operations
33 	
34 	The function passed to `unstable_cache` cannot depend on the incoming request. Read values from `cookies()` or `headers()` before calling the cached function, then pass those values as arguments so they become part of the cache key.
35 	
36 	The cached function also cannot:
37 	
38 	- Call `connection()`, which requires an incoming request
39 	- Enable or disable draft mode
40 	- Call `revalidateTag()`, `updateTag()`, or `revalidatePath()` during cache execution
41 	- Call a function that uses the `use cache: private` directive
42 	
43 	Perform request-dependent work before calling the cached function. Perform mutations and revalidation afterward from a Server Action or Route Handler.
44 	
45 	## Parameters
46 	
47 	```jsx
48 	const data = unstable_cache(fetchData, keyParts, options)()
49 	```
50 	
51 	- `fetchData`: This is an asynchronous function that fetches the data you want to cache. It must be a function that returns a `Promise`.
52 	- `keyParts`: This is an extra array of keys that further adds identification to the cache. By default, `unstable_cache` already uses the arguments and the stringified version of your function as the cache key. It is optional in most cases; the only time you need to use it is when you use external variables without passing them as parameters. However, it is important to add closures used within the function if you do not pass them as parameters.
53 	- `options`: This is an object that controls how the cache behaves. It can contain the following properties:
54 	  - `tags`: An array of tags that can be used to control cache invalidation. Next.js will not use this to uniquely identify the function.
55 	  - `revalidate`: The number of seconds after which the cache should be revalidated. Omit or pass `false` to cache indefinitely or until matching `revalidateTag()` or `revalidatePath()` methods are called.
56 	
57 	## Returns
58 	
59 	`unstable_cache` returns a function that when invoked, returns a Promise that resolves to the cached data. If the data is not in the cache, the provided function will be invoked, and its result will be cached and returned.
60 	
61 	## Example
62 	
63 	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
64 	import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache'
65 	
66 	export default async function Page({
67 	  params,
68 	}: {
69 	  params: Promise<{ userId: string }>
70 	}) {
71 	  const { userId } = await params
72 	  const getCachedUser = unstable_cache(
73 	    async () => {
74 	      return { id: userId }
75 	    },
76 	    [userId], // add the user ID to the cache key
77 	    {
78 	      tags: ['users'],
79 	      revalidate: 60,
80 	    }
81 	  )
82 	
83 	  //...
84 	}
85 	```
86

97 	    {
98 	      tags: ['users'],
99 	      revalidate: 60,
100	    }
101	  )
102	
103	  //...
104	}
105	```
106

108	
109	| Version   | Changes                      |
